scenes.title: From a ready pull request to main

cues.text: The merger takes a pull request from ready to merged.
One merger runs for each repository.
Only AI agents review. No person approves, and no outside review service takes part.
First, agents review the pull request and write one report.
Then a deterministic merge train rebases, tests and merges it.
Agents help in the train only when a rebase conflicts.

scenes.title: Webhooks, a safety poll, claims and a queue

cues.text: GitHub webhooks wake the merger: pull requests, check runs, workflow runs and pushes to main.
Each webhook wakes only the merger of its repository.
If a webhook is lost, a safety poll runs every 30 seconds.
cues.say: If a webhook is lost, a safety poll runs every thirty seconds.

cues.text: Two review workers run by default, beside one train loop and the main watch.
A heartbeat tells the API that the merger is alive.
A worker claims a pull request for two minutes, and renews the claim while it works.
If a pod dies, its claims expire, and another worker takes the pull request.
The queue takes bypassed pull requests first, then re-reviews, then first reviews.
In each group, the oldest ready pull request goes first.
A pull request is eligible when it is open, ready, based on main, and its head has a check run.
Before a review, the merger probes the model of each role.
The agent must read a secret value from a file and return it.
If a probe fails, the worker waits from one minute up to ten minutes.
Next come deterministic prechecks.
They catch fixup commits, large files, local paths, broken links and secrets.
The repository can add its own checks, such as a lint command.
Then reviewer agents read the diff in parallel lanes.
The default lanes are correctness, security and spec, and design.
A reviewer reports each finding through a tool call with a fixed schema.
An oracle on a different model checks the findings, four per call.
A finding blocks only when the reviewer and the oracle both grade it blocking.
These agents can only read and search. They cannot edit.

scenes.kicker: What it writes on the PR
scenes.title: One report, labels, and one draft at most

cues.text: During a review, the pull request has the in-audit label.
Each review ends in exactly one report comment.
Its title is Reviewed, Not merged, or Waiting for CI.
cues.say: Its title is Reviewed, Not merged, or Waiting for C I.

cues.text: Then come the merger, the head commit, the outcome, the CI line, and one section for each finding.
cues.say: Then come the merger, the head commit, the outcome, the C I line, and one section for each finding.

cues.text: If CI still runs, the merger posts the report now and parks the review.
cues.say: If C I still runs, the merger posts the report now and parks the review.

cues.text: When CI ends, it edits that same comment.
cues.say: When C I ends, it edits that same comment.

cues.text: Green CI hands the pull request to the train, with the reviewed label.
cues.say: Green C I hands the pull request to the train, with the reviewed label.

cues.text: A confirmed block, a rule break or red CI sends it back to the author.
cues.say: A confirmed block, a rule break or red C I sends it back to the author.

cues.text: The first time, it goes to draft with the review-requested label, and the ticket goes to Rework.
This happens once. A later block leaves the pull request ready.
A failed run writes no comment. Only the team channel hears about it.

scenes.title: Fixes, delta re-reviews and the arbiter

cues.text: The merger keeps watching after it sends a pull request back.
The author pushes a fix and marks the pull request ready.
Now it is a re-review, so it goes ahead of first reviews.
One reviewer reads only what changed since the reviewed head.
If the author rebased, the merger first replays the reviewed commits onto the new main.
So the delta does not contain the changes of main.
After the one rejection, a finding blocks only if it reopens an earlier one, or is a bug near the new changes.
A block that is confirmed again goes to an AI arbiter.
If the arbiter upholds it, the needs-maintainer label goes on, and a person decides.
If the arbiter dismisses every finding, the pull request goes on to the train.
If the author pushes during a review, the review stops. The next review covers only the push.
The train runs one step at a time, under a lease.
It takes first the pull request that overlaps least with the recent changes on main.
It rebases the branch onto main and pushes it with force-with-lease.
It waits for CI on that exact head. A webhook wakes it, and it also checks every 30 seconds.
cues.say: It waits for C I on that exact head. A webhook wakes it, and it also checks every thirty seconds.

cues.text: It merges only that tested head, posts a Merged comment, and deletes the branch.
When several pull requests wait, it chains up to four in a batch.
CI runs only on the top, and the members merge in order.
cues.say: C I runs only on the top, and the members merge in order.

cues.text: A red batch reruns its failed jobs once. Then it splits in halves until the bad pull request is alone.
If a rebase conflicts, a developer agent resolves it, and a reviewer agent checks the result.
Then the pull request gets a Rebased onto main comment and goes back to its place.
Before each effect, the train saves its intent, so a restart repeats nothing.
At hand-off, the ticket moves to Merging. After the merge, the tracker moves it to Done.
The main watch reads each finished CI run on main.
cues.say: The main watch reads each finished C I run on main.

cues.text: When main turns red, it opens one ticket with the logs of the failed jobs.
The ticket has the routing labels, so the daemon dispatches an agent to fix main.
When main is green again, it comments on the ticket and moves it to Done.
Both events also go to Slack or Discord.
Each repository sets its rules in a policy file.
The merger reads that file from main, so a pull request cannot weaken its own review.
The file sets the lanes, the checks, the merge method and the batch size.
Operators can bypass a review, requeue a pull request, or release a stuck claim.
They use the CLI, the API, or the Merger view in Tern.
cues.say: They use the C L I, the API, or the Merger view in Tern.

cues.text: Each merger agent is a live session that you can follow and interrupt.

scenes.title: Certified on a real GitHub repository

cues.text: The merger was certified on a real GitHub repository, with real CI and real agents.
cues.say: The merger was certified on a real GitHub repository, with real C I and real agents.

cues.text: A clean pull request merged at the reviewed head.
A real bug went back to draft once, with a confirmed finding.
Agents resolved a rebase conflict, and the pull request merged.
Batches of three merged with CI on the top only, also on a protected main.
cues.say: Batches of three merged with C I on the top only, also on a protected main.

cues.text: With no findings, a review took 10 to 40 seconds.
cues.say: With no findings, a review took ten to forty seconds.

cues.text: In the mocked runs, the merger reviewed and merged on both trackers.
